description: Shared permission-state source of truth. Create a new standalone, Mapbox-free, unit-testable module js/geo-permission.js (KPR.geoPermission) that reads geolocation permission state via navigator.permissions, exposes live subscription to its 'change' event, requests permission via a registered requester (never re-prompting when denied), and provides shared iOS detection. Wire js/map.js to register geolocateControl.trigger() as the requester and expose KPR.map.requestLocation(); de-duplicate the iOS detection in js/drive.js to call the shared helper. This feature is the foundation that FEAT-002 and FEAT-003 both depend on. It is independent of them and must leave the tree green on its own.
steps: Create js/geo-permission.js as an IIFE module `window.KPR = window.KPR || {}; KPR.geoPermission = (function(){ … })();` following the repo's module convention. Keep it dependency-free and free of any mapboxgl.* reference so tests/run.html can load it.

Implement internal state: a cached last-resolved state string, the current PermissionStatus object (once queried), a Set of subscriber callbacks, and a requester callback (default null). A guard helper returns true only when navigator.permissions && navigator.permissions.query && window.isSecureContext.
Implement getState() -> returns the cached state: one of 'granted' | 'prompt' | 'denied' | 'unsupported'. Initial cached value is 'unsupported' until init()'s query resolves.

Implement refresh() -> Promise<string>: if unsupported, resolve 'unsupported'; else navigator.permissions.query({name:'geolocation'}), store the PermissionStatus, update the cache, notify subscribers, resolve the new state. Swallow query rejections (resolve 'unsupported').
Implement subscribe(cb) -> adds cb to the Set and returns an unsubscribe function. Notify all subscribers with the current state on every 'change' event and after refresh().

Implement init(): if unsupported, leave state 'unsupported' and return; otherwise run refresh() and, on the resolved PermissionStatus, attach a 'change' listener that re-reads status.state into the cache and notifies subscribers. init() must be safe to call once at startup.
Implement setRequester(fn): store fn (used by map.js to register () => geolocateControl.trigger()).

Implement requestLocation(): if getState() === 'prompt' and a requester is set, call the requester and return true; otherwise return false. Must NOT call the requester when state is 'denied' or 'unsupported' (honors the browser constraint: a denied geolocation cannot be re-prompted from the page).

Implement isIOS(): copy the exact expression currently in js/drive.js _startGps(): /iPad|iPhone|iPod/.test(navigator.userAgent) || (navigator.platform === 'MacIntel' && navigator.maxTouchPoints > 1). Return the boolean.
Return { init, getState, refresh, subscribe, setRequester, requestLocation, isIOS } from the IIFE.

In js/map.js: after geolocateControl is created in _addLocateControl (or in init() once the control exists), call KPR.geoPermission.setRequester(() => geolocateControl.trigger()) and KPR.geoPermission.init(). Do NOT remove the existing denied-title tooltip behavior on the locate button — it is a safeguard. Add a public function requestLocation() that returns KPR.geoPermission.requestLocation(), and add requestLocation to the object returned by the KPR.map IIFE at the bottom.
In js/drive.js _startGps(): replace the inline iOS-detection regex expression with a call to KPR.geoPermission.isIOS(), leaving the surrounding PERMISSION_DENIED/TIMEOUT message logic unchanged.
Add <script src="js/geo-permission.js"></script> to index.html immediately BEFORE the <script src="js/map.js"></script> tag (map.js's init calls into geoPermission).
Add <script src="../js/geo-permission.js"></script> to tests/run.html (do NOT add map.js or drive.js to the harness — they need Mapbox).

Create tests/geo-permission.test.js mirroring tests/browse-routes.test.js structure. Because the harness runs in a real browser where navigator.permissions may exist, inject a stubbable seam: have the tests drive the module through a fake. Preferred approach: in geo-permission.js, read navigator.permissions through a tiny indirection the test can override (e.g. an internal _query function on the returned object for tests, OR accept the browser's real API and, in tests, temporarily replace navigator.permissions.query with a fake that resolves a fake PermissionStatus whose .state is settable and that supports dispatching a 'change'). Document whichever seam you choose in a comment. Assert: getState() reflects granted/prompt/denied; a simulated 'change' re-reads state and notifies subscribers; requestLocation() calls a spy requester only in 'prompt' and returns false (no call) in 'denied' and 'unsupported'; isIOS() returns expected booleans for representative userAgent/platform/maxTouchPoints inputs (stub navigator properties the same way the test stubs the seam).
Register tests/geo-permission.test.js at the end of the <script> list in tests/run.html.
acceptance_criteria: js/geo-permission.js exists, is a KPR.geoPermission IIFE, references no mapboxgl.* symbol, and loads in tests/run.html without a script error.
KPR.geoPermission exposes init, getState, refresh, subscribe, setRequester, requestLocation, isIOS.
requestLocation() invokes the registered requester only when state is 'prompt'; returns false and does not invoke it when state is 'denied' or 'unsupported'.
js/drive.js no longer contains a second copy of the iOS-detection regex in _startGps() (it calls KPR.geoPermission.isIOS()); the existing denied-title tooltip in map.js is unchanged.
Running the test command ends with RESULT: PASS and a total count greater than 304, with the new geo-permission test names listed as ok.
verification: Run: powershell -NoProfile -File tests\run-tests.ps1 — confirm the output ends with 'RESULT: PASS (N tests)' where N > 304 and the geo-permission tests show 'ok'. (Judge by the RESULT line; a non-zero exit from a QtWebEngine teardown message after PASS is benign.)

Grep-free confirmation that drive.js compiles/loads: the full suite loading drive.js is not in the harness, so additionally open index.html logic review — ensure js/geo-permission.js is listed before js/map.js in index.html script order.
findings:
DONE. Suite: RESULT: PASS (318 tests), up from baseline 304 (14 new geo-permission tests, all 'ok').

Public API as built — KPR.geoPermission (js/geo-permission.js, IIFE, Mapbox-free):
  init()            -> no-op when unsupported; else refresh() then attach a 'change' listener on the resolved PermissionStatus that re-reads status.state into the cache and notifies subscribers. Safe to call once at startup.
  getState()        -> cached string 'granted'|'prompt'|'denied'|'unsupported' (starts 'unsupported' until init's query resolves).
  refresh()         -> Promise<string>; re-queries, updates cache, notifies subscribers, resolves new state; resolves 'unsupported' when the Permissions API is absent/insecure or the query rejects.
  subscribe(cb)     -> adds cb to a Set, returns an unsubscribe fn. cb is called with the current state on every 'change' and after every refresh().
  setRequester(fn)  -> stores the requester (map.js passes () => geolocateControl.trigger()). Pass null to clear.
  requestLocation() -> calls the requester and returns true ONLY when getState()==='prompt' and a requester is set; otherwise returns false and does NOT call it (honors the browser's no-reprompt-on-denied rule; also false for 'unsupported').
  isIOS()           -> boolean; /iPad|iPhone|iPod/.test(navigator.userAgent) || (navigator.platform==='MacIntel' && navigator.maxTouchPoints>1). drive.js _startGps() now calls this instead of its inline regex.
  Support guard: navigator.permissions && navigator.permissions.query && window.isSecureContext.

Test seam used to stub navigator.permissions (see tests/geo-permission.test.js, mirrors browse-routes.test.js stubbing): the module reads navigator.permissions.query DIRECTLY (no internal indirection). Tests install stubs with Object.defineProperty(navigator,'permissions',{configurable:true,value:{query:()=>Promise.resolve(fakeStatus)}}) and force window.isSecureContext=true, tearing both down in a finally. fakeStatus has a settable .state plus addEventListener/removeEventListener('change',...) and a _fireChange(next) test helper that flips .state and invokes listeners (simulates the browser's live 'change'). The 'unsupported' path is driven by defining navigator.permissions=undefined. isIOS() inputs are stubbed the same way via Object.defineProperty on navigator.userAgent/platform/maxTouchPoints. Note navigator props are read-only in the browser runner, so defineProperty (not assignment) is required, and restore() deletes the own prop then re-applies any captured original descriptor.

Wiring in index.html: <script src="js/geo-permission.js"></script> is placed immediately BEFORE <script src="js/map.js"></script> (right after js/ocean-lut.js). The module's init() is NOT called from index.html — it is wired inside js/map.js _addLocateControl(), right after geolocateControl is created: KPR.geoPermission.setRequester(() => geolocate.trigger()); KPR.geoPermission.init();. So any later FEAT that needs permission state can rely on KPR.geoPermission being initialized once the map's locate control exists (map.init()). KPR.map also now exposes requestLocation() (delegates to KPR.geoPermission.requestLocation()) in the object returned at the bottom of the KPR.map IIFE. The existing denied-title tooltip on the locate button (map.js _addLocateControl's navigator.permissions.query ... _whenLocateButton) was left UNCHANGED (it is a safeguard).

tests/run.html: added <script src="../js/geo-permission.js"></script> (right after harness.js, before the other app modules) and registered <script src="geo-permission.test.js"></script> at the end of the test list. map.js and drive.js are intentionally still NOT in the harness (they need Mapbox).
